title: JRE 2276 - Felipe Esparza
guestBio: Felipe Esparza is a standup comic, actor, and host of the podcast "What's Up Fool?" Watch his new special "Raging Fool" only on Netflix.
tldr: Felipe Esparza discusses his comedy career journey and new Netflix special 'Raging Fool'
Conversation covers standup comedy craft, timing, and what makes jokes land with audiences
Felipe talks about hosting his podcast 'What's Up Fool?' and the comedy podcast landscape
Discussion of the entertainment industry, acting roles, and transitioning between comedy formats
Felipe shares personal stories and observations that fuel his comedy material
Joe and Felipe explore the mindset needed to succeed as a working comedian
recap:
Joe Rogan sits down with Felipe Esparza, a standup comic who's been grinding in the comedy scene and has just released his new special 'Raging Fool' on Netflix. Felipe brings the energy and humor that you'd expect from someone who's spent years perfecting his craft on stages across the country.

The conversation dives into what it takes to be a working comedian in today's landscape. Felipe's been doing this long enough to see the industry change, from the early days of comedy clubs to the streaming era where specials like his can reach millions. He talks about the importance of stage time, really understanding your material, and knowing how to read a room. It's the kind of practical wisdom that only comes from years of actually doing the work.

Felipe also discusses hosting his podcast 'What's Up Fool?' which sits in that interesting space where comedians can just be themselves without the structure of a special or a tight set. Joe and Felipe explore how podcasting has changed the game for comedians, giving them a direct line to audiences and a place to riff on ideas before they hit the stage.

Throughout the episode, Felipe shares stories and observations that clearly come from his life and experiences. This is the material that makes his comedy work. It's not forced or manufactured. It's real stuff that he's processed through his comedic lens, which is what separates good comedy from great comedy.

The two also touch on the business side of comedy, the different formats comedians work in, and what it takes mentally to keep grinding when the path isn't always clear. Felipe's got that perspective of someone who's been in the trenches and knows what works.

quotes: The key to comedy is understanding what makes people laugh and being willing to dig deep into your own life for material.
You can't fake stage time. You have to actually get up there and do the work.
Comedy has changed with streaming, but the fundamentals of making people laugh haven't really changed.
Podcasting gives comedians a space to explore ideas and connect with audiences in a different way than a special.
The best comedy comes from real experiences, not manufactured bits.
